children.text: The healthcare landscape in rural Vermont is currently grappling with a severe labor imbalance. Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) have seen a dramatic shift in their operational cost structures as the local workforce diminishes and the dependency on locum tenens staffing reaches unprecedented levels.

In parts of the Northeast Kingdom, a large share of clinical shifts are now covered by temporary locum staff. This dependency disrupts continuity of care and introduces significant price volatility into hospital budgets: the wage gap between full-time employees and contracted providers has widened to a point that threatens the long-term viability of small rural medical centers.

body.title: FY2024 Staffing Cost Comparison

children.text: The transition from a stable salaried workforce to a gig-economy model for specialized clinicians is the single greatest threat to hospital solvency in northern New England today.
To mitigate these risks, policy interventions must focus on regional retention incentives and the potential for state-wide staffing pools to counteract the premium rates charged by private agencies.

summary: This analysis examines the escalating reliance on temporary staffing within Vermont's Critical Access Hospitals, highlighting a 45% spending surge in FY2024. The resulting fiscal strain poses significant solvency risks for rural healthcare networks.
title: The Fiscal Impact of Locum Tenens Reliance in Rural Vermont
